cases.question: how long is the northern wren

cases.question: top speed of the carnelian liner

cases.question: what was the top speed of the pollux

cases.question: who was the first captain of the halcyon

cases.question: who is the master of the solway star

cases.question: what type of ship was the vigilant
cases.passage: The Vigilant was an armoured gunboat of the navy of Karsland, launched in 1874. She was built to defend the estuary of the Skel against raiding ships. Her single 25 centimetre gun was mounted in a revolving turret. She was hulked in 1902.

cases.question: when was the isolde grey sunk

cases.question: halstrom spirit tonnage

cases.question: how many crew did the fairweather have

cases.question: what is the bramble queen

cases.question: what was the gold venture named after

cases.question: how much can the hercules crane lift
cases.passage: The Hercules is a floating crane owned by the Port Kessel harbour authority. It can lift 1,600 tonnes in a single load. The crane was built in 1978 at the Lessing yard and refitted in 2004. It has been used to raise sunken ships and to place the sections of the Kessel Bridge.

cases.question: what fuel does the orvo stove use
cases.passage: The Orvo is a lightweight camping stove made by Halvern Outdoor. It burns paraffin, which is pumped under pressure to a brass burner. The stove was introduced in 1931 and weighs about 900 grams. It was carried on several polar expeditions in the 1930s.

cases.question: who invented the hollin hearing trumpet
cases.passage: The Hollin hearing trumpet is a folding ear trumpet made of silver plated brass. It was invented in 1834 by the surgeon Thomas Hollin, who was himself partly deaf. It could be folded small enough to carry in a waistcoat pocket. The trumpets were sold by the Hollin family until 1890.

cases.question: how deep can the nereid submersible dive
cases.passage: The Nereid is a crewed research submersible operated by the Ostmark Marine Institute. It can dive to a depth of 4,500 metres with a crew of three. The craft was launched in 1992 and was rebuilt with a new titanium hull in 2015. Its mother ship is the Northern Wren.

cases.question: what does the ferrous mantis robot do
cases.passage: The Mantis is a six-legged robot made by Ferrous Robotics. It inspects the inside of large pipes and tanks, crawling along the walls on magnetic feet. The robot carries cameras and an ultrasonic sensor that measures the thickness of the metal. It was first sold in 2019 to oil and water companies.

cases.question: when was the morrow mail clock introduced
cases.passage: The Morrow mail clock is a large wall clock made for post offices in the province of Morrow. It was introduced in 1868 so that every office would keep the same time as the central post office. The clocks were made by the firm of Pell and Lund. About 300 were made, and many survive in town museums.

cases.question: who is the current owner of the carrow lass
cases.passage: The Carrow Lass is a sailing barge built in 1897 for carrying grain along the coast. She was owned by the Pask family of millers for most of her working life. In 1961 she was sold to the artist Hugh Merrion, who lived aboard her for twenty years. She was then bought by a charter company and used for holidays. Since 2015 she has been owned by the Carrow Barge Trust, which restored her.
